extracted.intended_audience: media industry analysts, journalists, policymakers, and researchers interested in news media trends
extracted.subtask_description: Analysis and measurement of news media audience, revenue, staffing and distribution trends across newspapers, cable, local and network television, with definitions and methodological notes for comparing digital and broadcast metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total Digital Population (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Total Digital Population is the unduplicated combination of the desktop (web browsing + video) and mobile traffic figures (websites and associated apps).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because this is unduplicated, desktop and mobile figures combined may exceed the total digital population number; used as the basis for comparing desktop and mobile traffic to the total digital audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large gain/loss threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: A large loss or gain represents at least a 10% difference between 2014 and 2015.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied when classifying changes in traffic or minutes per visit between the two years; used to flag substantial change rather than nominal variation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison period for web traffic
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparison is between an average of October-December 2014 and October-December 2015.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysis uses Q4 averages to compare year-over-year performance for unique visitors and minutes per visit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entity matching homepage URL (comScore methodology)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each newspaper, the comScore entity matching its homepage URL was analyzed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures consistent mapping of comScore measurement entities to specific newspaper homepages when aggregating site-level traffic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average monthly unique visitors (metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average monthly unique visitors per newspaper website during the comparison period (Oct-Dec).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess reach; the report compares changes in unique visitors overall and separately for desktop and mobile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average monthly minutes per visit (metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average monthly minutes per visit for websites, measured separately for desktop and mobile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess engagement depth; minutes per visit can rise or fall independently of unique visitors and differs by platform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desktop vs. mobile unique visitors comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparison of unique visitors on desktop and mobile: e.g., for 39 of 50 sites desktop unique visitors fell while mobile rose for 43 of 50.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to detect platform shifts; report notes mobile unique visitors rose substantially while desktop often declined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform share threshold (mobile vs desktop)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mobile unique visitors exceeded desktop unique visitors by at least 10% for 44 of the 50 papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 10% margin is used as a practical threshold to indicate one platform substantially outpacing another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-spent platform comparison threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: For 41 of the 50 papers, average time spent per visit on desktop was 10% or greater than average time spent on mobile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses the 10% threshold to indicate materially higher engagement on desktop versus mobile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Web traffic-to-print-circulation ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: Average monthly unique visitors compared with average Sunday circulation (for 49 papers reporting Sunday circulation) — ranges from two to 78 times greater.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrates that web traffic far outpaces print circulation, but cautions that unique-visitor counts include many one-time visitors who may not be 'newspaper readers.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Visitor loyalty/engagement caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: Unique visitor counts do not distinguish single-article visitors from subscribers; a single-article visitor may be counted the same as a daily subscriber.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When diagnosing digital health, measure beyond raw unique visitors (e.g., frequency, depth, subscription conversions) because high traffic may include many 'grazers' who are not loyal readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of weighted annual averages (Nielsen)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nielsen provided weighted annual averages for network and cable viewership; weighted averages better account for slight differences in the number of programming hours in each broadcast month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weighted averages are preferred for year-over-year comparisons of broadcast viewership because they adjust for programming-hour differences; weighted vs unweighted differences here do not surpass 1.6% for the channels studied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prime-time viewership (cable news metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average prime-time viewership for CNN, Fox News and MSNBC (combined and individually).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prime time is the premier advertiser slot; the report presents combined and channel-level changes (e.g., combined prime-time up 8% to 3.1 million).

rubrics_metrics.name: Daytime viewership (6 a.m. – 6 p.m.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average daytime viewership measured between 6 a.m. and 6 p.m. for the three 24-hour cable news channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess non-prime viewing trends; the report shows daytime increases distributed across networks with percent changes by channel.

rubrics_metrics.name: 24-hour average viewership metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Total average viewership over a 24-hour period for the combined cable channels and for individual channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a holistic audience measure across all dayparts (e.g., combined 24-hour average increased 7% in 2015).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cable channel revenue composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Cable channels draw revenue from two main sources – advertising and subscriber (affiliate) fees, which come out of consumers’ monthly cable bills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revenue analysis separates these sources to show differing growth rates (e.g., Fox News projected subscriber fee growth vs. CNN ad growth).

rubrics_metrics.name: Projected revenue and profit figures (SNL Kagan)
rubrics_metrics.description: Projected annual revenue and profit figures for channels (e.g., Fox News, CNN, MSNBC) using SNL Kagan estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projections show percent growth and are used to compare channel financial performance; caution that these are projections and rely on SNL Kagan methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsroom spending (projection metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Projected newsroom spending totals for cable channels and financial networks (SNL Kagan projections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess investment in journalistic resources (e.g., combined newsroom spending for three main channels was projected to increase by 2% to $1.9 billion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign and domestic bureau counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of total domestic and foreign bureaus operated by news organizations (e.g., decline from 53 foreign bureaus in 2010 to 48 in 2015).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bureau counts are a proxy for international/newsgathering reach; updated numbers may vary by organization and reporting period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital presence and mobile visitation (comScore findings)
rubrics_metrics.description: comScore data showing mobile visitors driving a sizable share of traffic for cable news channels; during Q4 2015 all three channels drew more visitors from mobile devices than from desktop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Despite mobile visitor counts being higher, desktop visitors typically spend more minutes per visit; platform mix should be considered when evaluating digital engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of inorganic comScore entities (methodological note)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pew Research Center worked with comScore to identify and remove web entities whose traffic shifts over time were the result of inorganic changes in how those entities are measured, rather than organic audience behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This cleaning step is important to avoid misinterpreting measurement artifacts as real audience changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local TV viewership measurement (sweeps/quarter-hour audience)
rubrics_metrics.description: Viewership corresponds to the average of quarter-hour audience per time slot for each network and is based on the four sweeps (February, May, July and November).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of quarter-hour averages and sweep months standardizes local TV audience measurement; note that 2009 used March instead of February due to the digital transition affecting comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of news-producing stations
rubrics_metrics.description: News-producing stations are defined as those that have a news director and are viable, commercial and English-language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition was used to derive counts and revenue totals for news-producing stations (e.g., 833 stations in 2015).

rubrics_metrics.name: Share of local TV revenue from news programming
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage of local TV station revenue generated during news programming, based on RTDNA survey responses from news directors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as a share (about half of station revenue) and tracked year-over-year to show trends in revenue sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retransmission fees (definition and projection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Retransmission fees are the fees paid by cable and satellite systems to carry local channels; estimate projections (e.g., $6.3 billion in 2015, projected to reach $10.3 billion by 2021).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projections include O&O, affiliate station and reverse retransmissions and are a major contributor to local TV owner revenue growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political advertising revenue reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Political advertising revenues reported separately by major publicly held local TV station companies; used to track election-cycle-driven revenue changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparisons are made between election and non-election years and across company SEC filings to show political ad revenue trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average weekday local TV news hours
rubrics_metrics.description: Average amount of weekday local TV news programming (e.g., 5.3 hours per weekday in 2014, based on RTDNA survey).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess local news supply trends and whether news hours are increasing or holding steady.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local TV staffing and salary metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of full-time jobs in local television news and median newsroom salaries by role (Hofstra University survey data).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to measure workforce size and compensation trends (e.g., 27,600 full-time jobs, median salaries listed for specific roles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Local TV mergers & acquisitions value
rubrics_metrics.description: Total value of local TV mergers and acquisitions for a year (e.g., about $3 billion in 2015).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transaction totals include announced deals as of year-end and are updated annually; used to assess consolidation activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combined TV news magazine viewership metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Combined average viewership for network TV news magazine programs (e.g., six shows combined and year-over-year change).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregated to detect trends across long-form news magazine programming, which have shown sustained declines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising revenue estimates for network news programs (Kantar Media)
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated advertising revenues for evening and morning network news programs based on Kantar Media estimates (e.g., evening news up an estimated 6% for first three quarters of 2015).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to track financial performance of network news; estimates cover specified periods (e.g., Jan–Sept) and telecast types (e.g., Monday–Friday).
